name: axc-harness
description: Apply the repository's extracted coding harness to AXC implementation tasks, harness-readiness checks, and evaluation reporting. Distinguish native Codex work from the supplied Task A controller and preserve measurement evidence.
---

# AXC harness workflow

Resolve paths from the repository root. Read `openai-harness-v7.12.02/README.md` for the current controlled-upgrade workflow. For controller commands and frozen coding contracts, consult `openai-harness-v7.12.02/CODING_TASKS.md` and the selected task configuration. Read only relevant sections; do not ingest historical releases, logs, SHA manifests or Ollama reports as routine context.

## Choose the actual task and execution mode

- Read the task prompt and requirements named by the user completely. For the bundled AXC tasks these are `task-set-a-prompt.md` / `task-set-a-requirements.md` or `task-set-b-prompt.md` / `task-set-b-requirements.md` at the repository root. Their allowed/protected write boundaries govern feature work; user instructions take precedence.
- The shipped `coding-task-set-a.json`, `run_task_a.py` and independent course verifier are **Task A-specific**. Their presence does not establish a Task B controller or enrollment acceptance suite. For Task B, implement the supplied Task B specification natively and record its own tests and boundaries. Creating a controlled Task B preset is separate work; do not silently rename or reuse the Task A preset.
- The bundled Task A preset explicitly plans model, fixture storage and search in application services. That frozen historical plan conflicts with the current Cellix architecture profile: do not invoke it as the default controller for a Cellix feature evaluation. Native Task A/B work uses the fixed task requirements plus these repository skills. A separately approved Cellix controller profile and verifiers would be needed for controller-enforced execution; none is claimed by this integration.
- For an explicitly requested historical controlled adapter experiment, use its documented controller, provider ledger and review workflow, and disclose the fixture-oriented architecture profile. Do not start a provider/model experiment merely because the harness is installed.

## Before a measured implementation

Record the requested task ID, branch and exact starting commit. A comparison must use equivalent declared starting source and work scope; a completed feature is not a fresh implementation baseline. Keep raw run evidence in a new directory outside the measured checkout, as required by the controller. Run preparation only on a clean checkout with its declared runtime/dependencies; report failed prerequisites instead of silently repairing production or environment settings.

When usage measurement is requested, identify the original session and turn, capture the available cumulative counters and timestamp, and record a separate projection before substantive work. Include inspection, planning, implementation, validation and reporting in the declared scope. Preserve failed attempts and meaningful changes in scope.

## Implementation and verification

Before implementation or architecture review, read [the Cellix architecture skill](../cellix-architecture/SKILL.md). It is mandatory for the affected API/AXC/verification layers, including small catalogs and in-memory workflows. Its reference map and post-implementation review are completion evidence. The health-service pattern and fixture-only examples do not justify omitting domain or persistence responsibilities.

Follow existing `apps/api` composition, `packages/axc/rest` routes and application-service/domain/persistence package contracts. Keep vendor code and unrelated configuration unchanged. Prefer bounded source reads; retain a retrieval path when excerpts omit relevant material. Resolve failures with focused checks; do not repeat unchanged reads or validation without a new question or code change.

For feature completion run focused tests and the repository `pnpm run verify` gate, rather than treating a subset of passing checks as architectural acceptance. Its stages include lint/format policy, typecheck, build, Knip, dependency analysis, architecture, tests and security checks. The existing Turbo build inputs omit docs, so run `pnpm --filter @apps/docs build` directly after documentation changes. Readiness-only or documentation-only tasks do not require feature implementation or the entire application suite. Controller runs additionally use the frozen checks in their selected configuration. A review packet is not evidence that a review happened; report its actual status.

## Usage, assessment and handoff

Calculate native task usage as ending cumulative `total_token_usage` minus the counters at the starting boundary; never sum cumulative snapshots. Cached input is part of input, and reasoning output is part of output. Record explicit subagent usage separately when used and available; unknown counters remain unknown. Freeze the original turn boundary and exclude follow-ups. If final-response counters are pending, mark accounting incomplete and recover that original turn on the next user message before answering.

Provide implementation/source identity, relevant validation outcomes, limitations, separate measured/projection/cost fields and evidence locations. Read `openai-harness-v7.12.02/RUBRIC_POLICY.json` only when assessing scores or comparisons. Distinguish a qualified retrospective comparison from the policy's predeclared matched experiment. Historical test logs and mocked harness regressions are not new live-task results or measured savings.

name: cellix-architecture
description: Align AgentCourses implementation and review work with the local Cellix reference architecture. Use when changing or reviewing domain, application-service, persistence, REST/API composition, or architecture-test code in apps/api, packages/axc, or packages/axc-verification.
---

# Cellix Architecture Alignment

Use Cellix as an executable design reference, not merely as background documentation. Preserve the requested behavior while matching the applicable Cellix package boundaries and implementation patterns.

## Source Priority

Use an accessible Cellix checkout identified by the user or `CELLIX_REFERENCE_ROOT`, and record its commit. If none is available, consult <https://github.com/CellixJs/cellixjs> at an explicit revision. The verified navigation baseline is in [the source reference](references/source-reference.json). Existing AXC code is an example only when it demonstrably implements the same Cellix pattern; the health service and earlier fixture-only exercises are not architecture authority for a stateful workflow.

Do not modify the fixed task prompt to encode a solution. Do not copy an entire Cellix feature when only a smaller pattern is relevant.

## Workflow

### 1. Establish Constraints

- Read the applicable task requirements and allowed write boundary.
- Inspect the current AgentCourses packages and architecture tests.
- Identify existing behavior that must remain compatible.
- Check required workspace dependency edges before editing manifests, and keep declarations and the root lockfile synchronized. Do not introduce new external dependencies without task justification. If the fixed write boundary forbids a needed lockfile or directory change, surface that conflict and obtain a boundary exception rather than using undeclared imports or flattening layers. Preserve staged/user changes, including security and package-manager files.

### 2. Find the Nearest Cellix Vertical Slice

Search the local Cellix repository with `rg` and `rg --files`. Select a vertical slice by domain behavior and ownership, not by whichever package or filename is easiest to copy. Use an aggregate slice for a persisted business object with its own identity and lifecycle even if the current API only reads it. Use `packages/ocom/domain/src/domain/contexts/case/service-ticket/v1` as the primary mutation-workflow anchor when a concept is created, persists state transitions, records audit or history, owns nested lifecycle, or enforces transactional invariants. Use a read-model slice to implement queries, not to infer that the underlying domain object lacks future commands.

Read [the architecture map](references/architecture-map.md) to locate common reference patterns. Inspect the actual referenced source files and their sibling and parent `index.ts`, interface, repository, and test files before making design decisions because the source repository remains authoritative. For a stateful workflow, read the entire `persistence/src/datasources/domain/case/service-ticket-v1` slice, including adapter/converter, repository, unit of work, composition, and each focused test. Record the applicable reference tree and the planned destination tree, including suffixes, exports, and behavior; package-level similarity alone is insufficient.

### 3. Build an Alignment Map

Before editing, record this compact map in working notes:

| Responsibility | Project destination | Cellix reference | Decision or justified deviation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Concept classification by identity and lifecycle: aggregate, child entity, value object, or derived projection |  |  |  |
| API and application composition |  |  |  |
| Aggregate root, props, entity reference, and invariants |  |  |  |
| Value objects and child entities |  |  |  |
| Mutation repository and unit of work |  |  |  |
| Storage record, domain-props adapter, and converter |  |  |  |
| Repository creation, rehydration, and save conversion |  |  |  |
| Unit-of-work converter/repository wiring and persistence composition |  |  |  |
| Application operation |  |  |  |
| Read repository contract and implementation |  |  |  |
| Domain data source or repository implementation |  |  |  |
| Entity, context, data-source, and package exports |  |  |  |
| Application-facing types and errors |  |  |  |
| Transport |  |  |  |
| Tests by owning layer and composed public path |  |  |  |
| Contract documentation, when required |  |  |  |

Choose a context name before filling the map, then carry it through domain, application services, persistence, data-source namespaces, and public API types. Classify each concept before choosing its files. A persisted business object with independent identity and lifecycle is an aggregate by default, including when its current API only exposes queries. Reserve derived projection for a view with no independent domain identity or lifecycle, and record evidence for that classification. An aggregate needs a static `getNewInstance` factory that establishes valid initial state, props, entity reference, applicable value objects, exports, and focused tests; defer mutation-side contracts and adapters only when commands are outside the current task, recording the deferred responsibilities. Keep reconstruction of stored objects distinct from creation through this factory. A command concept with creation plus state transitions, audit or history, nested lifecycle, or transactional invariants uses the full applicable aggregate pattern. List every applicable reference file, test companion, or behavior intentionally omitted, so missing pieces are deliberate rather than accidental. Complexity, implementation speed, and a passing transport test do not justify omission.

### 4. Implement by Layer

- **Composition:** Wire services, data-sources factories, and handlers in `apps/api`; pass the factory through `ApiContext` to the application-services host. Keep feature logic elsewhere. The host must not construct a concrete persistence adapter itself.
- **Domain:** Put every named business concept, its props, entity reference, invariants, applicable value objects, and exports under `packages/axc/domain/src/domain/contexts/<context>/<entity>/`, even when all exposed operations are queries. Model an independently identified, persisted business object with Cellix `AggregateRoot` and `*.aggregate.ts` by default; use `DomainEntity` for a child entity or another behaviorally justified case, never solely because there is no write endpoint. For commands, match the selected Cellix `*.repository.ts`, `*.uow.ts`, child-entity, visa or passport, event, `index.ts`, and focused-test responsibilities that apply. Use `@cellix/domain-seedwork` aggregate, entity, repository, and unit-of-work abstractions instead of project-local reductions. Do not expose a mutable record plus free mutation functions as the domain model.
- **Application services:** Organize context and entity APIs below `src/contexts/<context>/<entity>`. Put each public operation in its own file, where its application-owned command or query input is declared beside a curried factory such as `(dataSources: DataSources) => async (query) => result`. Keep entity `index.ts` to a named service interface and operation composition. Follow Cellix context composition: import an entity API with an alias and its explicit service type (for example, `Course as CourseApi, type CourseApplicationService`), then expose a named context service interface. `DataSources` may be imported from persistence for injection; persistence query, page, filter, and repository types must not define public application-service contracts. Domain entity references may be returned when the selected Cellix slice does so.
- **Queries:** Read through `readonlyDataSource` rather than owning records in the application service.
- **Mutations:** Use the domain data source and scoped transaction pattern when persistence is involved. Load and mutate the aggregate through its domain repository inside the unit of work; application services orchestrate and do not reproduce aggregate transition rules.
- **Persistence:** Put read-side repository interfaces and implementations under `packages/axc/persistence/src/datasources/readonly/<context>/<entity>/<entity>.read-repository.ts`, with applicable entity, context, and data-source `index.ts` composition and `*.data.ts` when a separate data source is needed. Keep fixtures behind that boundary. For command aggregates, mirror the selected Cellix domain data-source adapter, converter, repository, unit-of-work, composition, and semantic tests under the corresponding domain data-source path. `*.domain-adapter.ts` must adapt a stored record to the domain props contract and provide or pair with a converter that constructs the aggregate from stored state and an adapter for new aggregate creation. The mutation repository must use this boundary for `getNewInstance`, retrieval, and save; the unit of work must wire the converter and repository, and the entity `index.ts` must expose the initialized unit of work. An in-memory store is a storage technology substitution, not an adapter/converter substitution. Do not place a `*ReadRepository` interface in domain; Cellix's domain `*.repository.ts` files serve a different, mutation-side role. Do not collapse applicable composition levels into the root factory merely because the resulting object has the correct shape.
- **REST:** Keep validation and HTTP error mapping at the transport boundary. Application failures carry stable codes and details without HTTP status numbers; REST maps those codes to response statuses. Register feature routes from modules below `src/features`; do not grow the package entry point into a feature implementation. Production transport code must not import persistence contracts. Prefer application-service public contracts or transport-local request types over domain imports unless the chosen Cellix reference establishes a direct domain dependency.
- **Tests:** Put aggregate transition and invariant tests beside the aggregate, and value-object boundary tests beside the value objects. Test application orchestration and persistence semantics separately, then prove public behavior through the composed HTTP acceptance path. Assert specified error status and code together. Verify material state and audit fields directly. For command persistence, add focused adapter/converter, repository, unit-of-work, and composition tests: cover stored-to-domain and domain-to-stored round trips, nested history or child data, repository factory creation, retrieval and save, and transaction behavior. When an in-memory or other custom adapter replaces the reference implementation, also test the applicable observable semantics, such as commit, rollback, isolation, serialization, and defensive copying.
- **Documentation:** When required, account for every affected endpoint or public operation, including inputs, successful outputs, status or result, and specified errors. Derive this checklist from the task rather than adding a generic documentation burden to every change.

### 5. Review Against Cellix

Read and complete [the alignment review](references/review-template.md). Compare the planned, reference, and implemented trees as well as filename suffixes, folder depth, interfaces, seedwork inheritance, aggregate and value-object semantics, exports, persistence adapters, feature behavior, tests, context names, and dependency direction. Treat unexplained structural or semantic differences and missing applicable pieces from the chosen Cellix references as defects. Do not treat a passing functional test suite as proof of architectural alignment.

### 6. Verify

Run focused tests while implementing, then run the repository completion gate from `AGENTS.md`. Architecture-test failures must be fixed in application code; do not weaken the guardrail to make a feature pass.

Reuse the alignment map and completed review during final verification. Run shared build-dependent completion commands sequentially and avoid repeating unchanged successful checks; follow [the harness workflow](../axc-harness/SKILL.md) for scope and security checks. Follow the task's explicit reporting requirements.

## Guard against the reported failure

A file-count limit or a small fixed catalog is not a reason to put aggregate invariants, status history mutation, concrete storage maps or repository construction into application services. For Task B, enrollment creation, status transitions, duplicate-active checks and audit history require an explicit domain/persistence/application mapping. A `catalog.ts` or `enrollment.ts` in the application-service root may orchestrate operations, but cannot substitute for those owning layers.

Do not accept a passing endpoint suite as architectural proof. Before completion, compare the implemented tree and semantics with the planned reference map. Missing applicable aggregate, value-object, adapter/converter, repository, unit-of-work, composition, export or focused-test responsibilities are unresolved findings. An approved behavior-based deviation may be documented; speed, fewer files and preserving a fixture example do not justify it. Do not add real authentication, MongoDB infrastructure or unrelated Cellix features when the sample task excludes them.

item.text:
**The proposed code cannot be accepted under the repository’s current architecture requirements.** Enrollment has independent identity, creation, transitions, and audit history, so the required reference is Cellix’s stateful aggregate workflow.

I verified the local Cellix checkout at `0dda578701214d524dd961849c9ae3e39f882834`. This was a source-only review; no files were modified, builds/tests run, providers launched, or report files created.

The acceptance-blocking findings are:

1. **Domain behavior is implemented in application services.** In [enrollment-requests.ts:12](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/axc/packages/axc/application-services/src/enrollment-requests.ts:12), `EnrollmentRequest` is a mutable record. Lines 54–68 define validation and transitions; lines 95–104 establish identity, pending state, and initial history; lines 125–131 enforce rejection/transition rules and mutate history/status. These responsibilities require a domain aggregate with props, entity reference, `getNewInstance`, constrained value objects, and aggregate-owned lifecycle methods. The inspected domain source tree contains only `src/index.ts`, with no enrollment implementation.

2. **Application services own concrete persistence and bypass the required conversion/transaction boundaries.** [enrollment-requests.ts:74](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/axc/packages/axc/application-services/src/enrollment-requests.ts:74) creates a `Map`; retrieval, duplicate lookup, filtering, and writes operate directly on it at lines 76–79, 91–105, 114–118, and 132. There is no storage-record/props adapter, converter, mutation repository, initialized unit of work, or read repository. Synchronous execution and defensive cloning provide useful behavior but do not satisfy those architectural responsibilities. Duplicate-active checking and creation must be coordinated through the persistence transaction boundary.

3. **Composition constructs storage inside the application host.** [application-services/src/index.ts:51](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/axc/packages/axc/application-services/src/index.ts:51) invokes the storage-owning factory. `ApiContext` contains only `environment`, and [apps/api/src/index.ts:9](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/axc/apps/api/src/index.ts:9) supplies no data-sources factory. API composition must create/inject persistence through context; the application host consumes it.

4. **HTTP policy and request validation leak into application services.** [enrollment-requests.ts:31](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/axc/packages/axc/application-services/src/enrollment-requests.ts:31) embeds HTTP status numbers in `EnrollmentError`. Lines 45–61 parse untyped request values, and public mutation methods accept `unknown`. [enrollment-routes.ts:8](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/axc/packages/axc/rest/src/enrollment-routes.ts:8) also constructs that HTTP-bearing application error; [rest/src/index.ts:11](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/axc/packages/axc/rest/src/index.ts:11) forwards its status. REST must parse/validate requests and map stable application error codes to HTTP statuses. Domain invariants still require domain enforcement.

5. **The feature lacks the required context/entity organization and operation contracts.** [enrollment-requests.ts:82](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/axc/packages/axc/application-services/src/enrollment-requests.ts:82) implements all operations inline in a root-level factory, with an inferred service type at line 137. Required equivalents are separate curried operation files below `src/contexts/<context>/<entity>`, named entity/context interfaces, and composition exports. [enrollment-routes.ts:11](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/axc/packages/axc/rest/src/enrollment-routes.ts:11) is correctly separated from the REST entrypoint, but must reside below `src/features`.

6. **The available tests do not establish layer-specific compliance.** [enrollment.test.mjs:22](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/axc/packages/axc-verification/enrollment-tests/enrollment.test.mjs:22) exercises composed HTTP behavior, and line 151 checks copying through the application factory. There are no enrollment aggregate/value-object, orchestration, adapter/converter, repository, or unit-of-work tests in the inspected owning layers. The architecture suite checks dependency boundaries; it does not establish the missing aggregate/persistence structure. No passing result is inferred.

The responsibility map from the inspected Cellix sources is below. Reference paths are relative to `cellix-reference/packages/ocom`; destination paths are relative to `axc/packages/axc`. `enrollment` is a proposed consistent context name, not an existing implementation.

| Responsibility inspected | Cellix reference | Required destination |
|---|---|---|
| Identity, initial state, transitions, audit ownership | `domain/src/domain/contexts/case/service-ticket/v1/`: aggregate, value objects, activity-detail entity, repository/UOW contracts, exports and focused test excerpts | `domain/src/domain/contexts/enrollment/enrollment-request/`: aggregate, props/reference, factory, value objects, history model, seedwork contracts and tests |
| Stored-state adaptation and reconstruction | Entire `persistence/src/datasources/domain/case/service-ticket-v1/` slice, including converter/adapter and focused tests/features | `persistence/src/datasources/domain/enrollment/enrollment-request/`: record/props adapter and converter, including history round trips |
| Creation, retrieval, save, UOW wiring | Same slice’s repository, UOW, entity composition, tests; parent case/domain composition | Same destination’s `*.repository.ts`, `*.uow.ts`, entity/context/data-source exports and semantic tests |
| Queries and filtering | `persistence/src/datasources/readonly/community/community/` repository/data/composition and parent indexes | `persistence/src/datasources/readonly/enrollment/enrollment-request/`, composed through `readonlyDataSource` |
| Typed use-case orchestration | `application-services/src/contexts/service/service/create.ts` and entity/context indexes; `user/end-user/query-by-name.ts` | `application-services/src/contexts/enrollment/enrollment-request/`: separate create/get/list/change-status operations |
| Dependency injection | Cellix `apps/api/src/index.ts`, application-services host, persistence data-source factories | AXC API/context creates and injects data-sources factory |
| Transport | `rest/src/index.ts`, plus repository-specific REST requirements | `rest/src/features/...`: request validation, application delegation, HTTP mapping |

Enrollment history has no specified independent identity or lifecycle; a domain-owned immutable value representation can justify omitting Cellix’s identified activity child entity. MongoDB/ObjectIds, population, messaging/search infrastructure, and real authentication are unnecessary for this sample. Those omissions do **not** justify omitting aggregate, conversion, repository, or transaction responsibilities.

Two boundary decisions are prerequisites to remediation:

- [Task B prompt:23](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/harness-only-1b/task-set-b-prompt.md:23) and [requirements:45](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/harness-only-1b/task-set-b-requirements.md:45) prohibit additional directories, while current guidance requires context/entity directories absent from this implementation. An explicit directory-boundary exception is required before implementing that layout.
- Required workspace dependency edges are absent: application services → persistence/domain, persistence → domain, and API → persistence. Adding them requires synchronized manifest and root `pnpm-lock.yaml` changes; the fixed allowed paths exclude the root lockfile. That also requires an explicit boundary exception.

The current [Cellix skill:23](/Users/dfortun/Documents/Codex/2026-10-21/read-both-task-a-documents-and-4/work/harness-only-1b/.agents/skills/cellix-architecture/SKILL.md:23) expressly requires surfacing these conflicts rather than flattening the layers. The historical Task A preset provides no exception.
